doctrines.title: Evolve schemas and stored documents by versioned, idempotent, probed steps
doctrines.statement: Schema and document change is a first-class engineering surface: every migration step probes the live schema (not a version counter), runs its multi-statement batch in an explicit transaction, and is safe to re-run. Anything persisted outlives the validation that wrote it, so stored documents carry a version and are read through tolerant parsers that migrate forward and merge over fresh defaults. Forbidden: relying on CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS to add columns, startup-only one-shot migration rituals, and overwriting user-edited seeded files without a version-stamp check.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failure class is the half-applied or silently-skipped change — CREATE IF NOT EXISTS skipping a late column on every install that matters; a crash mid-DDL leaving schema that idempotency probes then misread; an app replaying its whole migration chain in place so one bad step strands the user inside a half-migrated file (hence: snapshot the DB file before the pool opens); historical rows holding values current input rules would reject. **Tensions**: probing live schema costs boot time vs trusting a version counter that lies after partial upgrades; dual-write transition phases keep the old column canonical, trading temporary underreporting for zero corruption; tolerant read parsers risk masking real bugs, so tolerance is scoped (the dual-shape reader is deliberately limited to the one ambiguous field).

Governs:
- CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never adds columns — pair every late column with an ignore-error ALTER
- Wrap multi-statement DDL in an explicit transaction — SQLite autocommits per statement
- Stage a column-to-child-table migration as numbered ADR steps: dual-write best-effort while the old column stays canonical
- Track applied migrations in a table and make the run idempotent
- Make each migration idempotent by probing the live schema
- Disable foreign keys before the transaction, restore with a guard
- Enforce late-added column bounds with ABORT triggers when ALTER cannot add a CHECK
- Copy the database file before the connection pool opens it
- Upgrade a seeded user-editable file only on a stored version bump
- Version every persisted document and sanitise it on read
- Migrate stored settings forward, then deep-merge over defaults
- Collapse scattered localStorage keys into one versioned document with sync reads over async hydration
- Centralize a dual-shape reader for a field two writers shipped differently — scoped to that field only
triggers: adding a column to an existing table
changing the shape of a persisted JSON document
seeding files the user can edit
reading old rows written by previous versions

doctrines.title: Put all persistence behind one seam, and write down every tier choice
doctrines.statement: Every SQL statement, pool, and driver lives behind a single store interface composed from narrow per-domain repositories; the concrete driver is resolved lazily inside one cached accessor, and the boundary is enforced by lint rules, not by convention. Storage-tier choices (client vs server, localStorage, a separate DB file for user-writable data, even git-as-store) are legitimate only when stated as a written decision at the boundary. Forbidden: inline SQL in command handlers, per-module connection pools, per-driver forked query strings, and caching the absence of a driver.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: six independent projects in this workspace converged on the same arrangement, and the recorded failures all come from leaks around it — a subsystem issuing raw queries nobody can migrate with shared tooling; pools drifting in exactly the settings that matter; two concurrent cold starts each opening a single-connection embedded DB because the accessor awaited before assigning its cache; a cached null disabling persistence for the whole process after late-arriving config; connection-scoped SQLite extensions silently missing on pool-cached connections. **Tensions**: physical isolation (a separate DB file for agent-writable data) costs a second pool but buys corruption isolation; a stated client/server split costs an ADR but stops every new module re-deciding by imitation; parity between divergent backend shapes needs a documented interface note plus a parity test, because nothing else forces both drivers to honour one contract.

Governs:
- Put all persistence behind one store interface and a lazy driver
- Commit to one SQL dialect so drivers never fork the query strings
- Consolidate every connection into one pool with one tuning point
- Keep every SQL statement behind a repository module
- Register every feature's storage through one shared store factory
- Make the client/server storage split a stated rule, not a precedent
- Compose the store interface from narrow per-domain repositories
- Select the persistence driver lazily behind one cached accessor
- Enforce the persistence boundary in the linter, then test the rule
- Never cache a 'no driver configured' result — let late config heal
- Assign the store promise before the first await, not after it
- Register connection-scoped extensions BEFORE the pool exists — they only apply to new connections
- Give user-writable data its own database file and pool, fully isolated from app state
- Say so at the interface when two backends model a concept differently
- Use localStorage as a deliberate, bounded, single-module persistence tier with an inline ADR
- Use git itself as the per-turn snapshot/rollback store for agent-edited projects
triggers: writing a new query or repository
choosing where a new kind of data lives

doctrines.title: Persist canonical machine keys and closed vocabularies, never display strings
doctrines.statement: Identity and classification live in canonical, machine-shaped values: closed vocabularies from one enforcing source, collision-safe generated ids, content-derived ids for regenerated results, explicit tags for 'active'. Human-readable labels are presentation only — never persisted as values, never scanned to reconstruct ownership, and used as an attribution fallback only when a name maps to exactly one owner. Forbidden: linking derived entities by searching display text, selecting the current version by max(version_number), and Date.now()-only id generation.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are silent misattribution and identity collapse — substring scans over descriptions cross-linking every service whose name is contained in another; a rolled-back version re-selected forever by max(version_number) (an infinite rollback loop); Date.now ids colliding the moment an AI agent batches creations in one tick; re-deriving a discovered item's source at import re-running the last-writer-wins scan and importing a value the user never approved; author-chosen metadata axes fragmenting into noise when left open. **Tensions**: closed vocabularies need an 'unsorted' quarantine shelf or they silently drop reality; taxonomies must be built from a scan of the real corpus, not intuition, or they orphan the actual data; the display-name fallback is sometimes genuinely the only signal — the discipline is the collision set, not a total ban.

Governs:
- Close every author-chosen metadata axis, and delete the axis that cannot discriminate
- Pair every settings key with a _DEFAULT constant and encode the unit in the key name
- Validate settings keys and values inside the repository itself
- Resolve a config cascade once into per-field {value, source, isOverridden} provenance and render inheritance from that shape
- Keep persisted values canonical English and translate only labels
- Build a browse taxonomy from a scan of the real corpus
- Link derived entities by index or identity, never by scanning display strings
- Fall back from id-attribution to display-name matching only when the name maps to exactly one owner
- Date.now()-only ids collide the moment a second writer or a same-millisecond batch appears
- Encode the exact winning source into a discovered item's id; never re-derive at import
- Identify the active version by an explicit tag, never by max(version_number)
- Give repeatable analysis results a content-derived stable id
triggers: designing an id or key scheme
adding a status or category field

doctrines.title: Derive computable values; keep unknown as unknown, never fabricate
doctrines.statement: A value that can be computed from existing data should be a pure derived function, not a stored copy that drifts when one writer forgets it. Not-known is a modelled state: keep the unknown sentinel through ingestion and analysis, surface the gap to the reader, and distinguish 'user declined' from 'never asked'. Forbidden: interpolating missing data into plausible numbers, self-reported metadata where structure can be computed, and caching a derived value without owning its invalidation.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: stored duplicates drift silently, and fabricated completeness corrupts every aggregate downstream — an interpolated timestamp or estimated price makes a dataset look whole while quietly poisoning it; self-reported difficulty/setup-time attributes go stale and get gamed; an unpinned catalog instance flagged as stale produces a false update nag worse than silence. **Tensions**: derivation costs compute on every read — cache only when measurably hot, and then own invalidation explicitly; derived catalog scores must cap each term and snap to buckets so an estimate does not masquerade as a measurement; explicit-empty-vs-null costs one extra convention but is the only way later logic can tell a decision from an absence.

Governs:
- Derive the value instead of storing a copy that can drift
- Leave unknown values unknown and report the gap to the user
- Compute catalog metadata from structure, don't ask authors for it
- Store money as integer minor units and convert at one seam
- Pin the source version at adoption so drift is provable
- Persist an explicit empty value for 'user declined', reserving null for 'never asked'
triggers: adding a computed or summary column

doctrines.title: One encoding per timestamp column; normalize to UTC at shared chokepoints
doctrines.statement: A timestamp's encoding is a property of the column, not of the code reading it: compare cutoffs in the exact encoding the column was written in, normalize unzoned SQLite datetimes to explicit UTC at one shared chokepoint, and parse mixed formats to epoch before any comparison. Semantically distinct moments get distinct columns — human adjudication gets its own decidedAt, a stamped baseline is written once server-side, and time buckets anchor on the data's own dates, never the client clock.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are all silent misorderings — SQLite's bare 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' misread as local time so fresh rows display as hours old; lexicographic compares misordering the moment RFC3339 and naive shapes mix; a retention-sweep cutoff whose separator sorts after every digit classifying a whole day wrong, invisibly deleting data; background maintenance touching updatedAt and resurfacing months-old decisions as this week's news; client-clock bucketing mislabelling the head bucket across timezone boundaries. **Tensions**: one chokepoint formatter is a small refactor tax every reader must pay, but scattering per-caller fixes guarantees at least one diverges; monotonic-clock state can survive restarts only via wall-clock conversion under a short TTL — stale transient state is worse than starting fresh.

Governs:
- Normalize unzoned SQLite datetimes to explicit UTC before Date parsing
- Parse timestamps to epoch before comparing when the backend mixes formats
- Compare timestamps in the encoding the column was written in
- Anchor time buckets on the data's own dates, not the client clock
- Give human adjudication its own timestamp, distinct from the row's updatedAt
- Stamp the scope baseline once at activation and derive scope creep from it server-side
- Persist monotonic-clock state across restarts via elapsed-to-wall-clock conversion under a short TTL
triggers: formatting relative time in the UI

doctrines.title: Every list read is bounded, and its filters and counts live in the query
doctrines.statement: A default limit is part of the repository contract — an unbounded read must be asked for explicitly. Filters, facet counts, and exclusions are pushed into SQL, because a client-side filter over a paged stream lets a chatty category starve every other one and renders low-volume lenses empty over thousands of matching rows. Pagination cursors over second-resolution timestamps are composite (timestamp, id), and incremental log mining carries a per-file watermark with an explicit exhausted flag.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are page-boundary loss and starvation — a timestamp-only keyset cursor dropping rows when a burst shares one second; machine-written events (57 percent of one log) crowding conversation down to 2 of 20 recall slots until the exclusion moved into SQL; a WHERE status='completed' predicate on rows that speak a different status vocabulary silently emptying every rollup (predicate on evidence presence instead); one unbounded query among bounded siblings staying invisible until the table grows. **Tensions**: pushing filters down duplicates a little logic per query but is the only honest source for counts; serving from a stored excerpt kills a per-row N+1 only when a shared cap constant proves completeness — writer truncation cap and reader check must be the same constant.

Governs:
- Give every list query a default bound, no exceptions
- Push the filter into the query — a filtered page starves categories
- Keyset pagination over second-resolution timestamps needs a composite (at, id) cursor
- Keyset-page on a total order, and serve from the stored excerpt only when a shared cap constant proves it is complete
- Exclude machine/correlator records from a recall window in SQL, so the window fills instead of shrinking
- Result rows and run rows speak different status vocabularies — predicate on evidence presence, not a status literal
- Mine append-only logs incrementally with a per-file byte watermark
triggers: writing a list or feed query
adding a filter or facet rail

doctrines.title: Status writes are guarded transitions that name their expected source state
doctrines.statement: Any write that changes lifecycle state names the states it may apply from — conditional updates, compare-and-swap, one shared FSM — and returns whether it applied rather than throwing when a legitimate race loses. Terminal states are asymmetric sinks: a completion landing after a user's Stop must never resurrect success. Prerequisites are acquired before the run row is inserted, load-bearing writes fail loudly while telemetry writes are explicitly best-effort, and restored state rehydrates into shapes the system already knows how to wake.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are illegal transitions under racing writers — a completion clobbering a freshly-written cancel back to 'completed' (lost-cancel plus success theater); double-submits and stale tabs performing transitions no FSM allows; run rows orphaned forever in their initial status because auth resolution failed after insert; two 'different-level' flows touching the same columns without real mutual exclusion; a skipped scheduler tick stamping last-fired for a fire that never happened. **Tensions**: returning applied/not-applied pushes handling onto callers but is the only honest shape when races are legitimate; a declarative macro stamping N parallel run/result tables trades a little indirection for one FSM fixed once for every mode; classifying writes as load-bearing vs telemetry must be visible at the call site or the split erodes.

Governs:
- Apply status changes conditionally on the status you expect
- Two flows that write the same columns need real mutual exclusion
- Cancellation is a terminal sink: a result landing after Stop must never resurrect success
- A skipped tick advances the schedule pointer but must never stamp 'last fired'
- A proposal queue against a moving target keeps exactly one pending row: filing a new one supersedes the old in the same transaction
- Acquire every prerequisite before inserting the run row
- Classify each write as load-bearing or telemetry, and encode the difference at the call site
- Stamp N parallel run/result table pairs from one declarative macro so every repo shares one CRUD and one status FSM
- Rehydrate persisted sessions as an already-existing sleep state, not a new restore state

doctrines.title: Destroy nothing by default: demote, tombstone, dry-run, allowlist
doctrines.statement: Deletion is the last resort and never the default: forget by demotion through one shared statement every read path filters on, soft-delete disputed evidence, and make removed seed rows a status change so re-seeding cannot resurrect them. Destructive sweeps default to dry-run, delete only allow-listed terminal states (never NOT IN — an unknown state is never deleted), pair age cutoffs with count caps scoped to the same terminal set, and derive retention cutoffs from the largest live window rather than a constant. Before any destructive apply, re-derive keep/delete from the user's resolution and assert they differ.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failure class is unrecoverable loss that reports success — a DELETE-based forget that a search lane does not honour so forgetting never binds; deleted seed rows silently reappearing on the next boot; a hardcoded retention cutoff racing any consumer whose window exceeds it; append-only undo journals that must exclude run records (undo erasing evidence a run happened) and credentials (undo resurrecting a revoked secret). **Tensions**: demotion keeps rows and files around — the cost is storage and the discipline that every read path filters the demotion predicate, or forgetting only affects some views; dry-run-by-default adds one operator step to every real prune, which is exactly the point; before-image journaling needs a curated allowlist because some tables make undo a hazard, not a safety net.

Governs:
- Prune dry-run by default, allowlist terminal states, clamp the age floor
- Forget by demotion through one shared statement that every read path filters on — never DELETE
- Seed vocabularies with INSERT OR IGNORE so re-seeding cannot resurrect operator changes; demote by status, never delete
- Soft-delete evidence rows and append rather than edit consent
- Journal reversible writes as before-images through an allowlisted preupdate hook — and exclude tables where undo is a hazard
- Pair the age cutoff with a count cap, both scoped to terminal rows
- Re-derive keep/delete from the user's resolution and assert they differ before a destructive apply
- Derive a suppression-cache's retention cutoff from the largest live window, not a constant
triggers: writing a delete or cleanup path

doctrines.title: Assume concurrent writers: merge at the store, re-read before every write
doctrines.statement: Any document can have a second writer — autosave, an assistant, another tab, another device — so partial updates merge at the database level, never via application read-modify-write, and a record hydrated from a lean list projection is never written back without a fresh re-read. Upserts are real upserts (unique constraint or one process-wide lock; select-then-insert is not idempotent under concurrency), patch shapes distinguish omit from clear, and blank inputs in write-only secret forms mean unknown, never clear. Cross-device sync lands deltas in a staged inbox with one reconciler, syncs deletions as explicit tombstones, and resolves same-user conflicts with a coordination-free deterministic tiebreak.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failure class is the silent clobber — writing an edited record from a list row wiping the heavy fields the projection blanked; a panel that fell back to empty defaults on load failure persisting those defaults over the real config on the next save (a security regression when the config is policy); two overlapping check-then-insert passes both observing absence and duplicating every row; hard deletes without tombstones resurrecting on the next device pull; blanks in a secrets form wiping OAuth tokens the form could never display. **Tensions**: DB-level merge must be stated at the interface because the wrong layer is exactly where the pre-read creeps back in; autosave needs a small derived slice, debounce, and unmount flush — writing raw in-memory state produces constant stale snapshots; content-deduped publishers must stamp timestamps at write time or the timestamp defeats the dedupe.

Governs:
- Merge partial updates in the database, never read-modify-write
- Never write back a record hydrated from a lean list projection — re-read the full record right before the merge-write
- Select-then-insert is not an upsert — constrain it or serialise it
- Upsert on a nullable natural-key column via a UNIQUE expression index over COALESCE(col, '')
- Use a nullable-patch shape so omit and clear are distinguishable
- In write-only secret forms, a blank input means 'unknown', never 'clear'
- Refuse to save a config whose load failed
- Autosave by diffing a small derived slice, debounced, flushed on exit
- Content-dedupe a debounced publisher by stamping timestamps at write time, not build time
- Same-user device sync: three-way merge with first-class tombstones and a coordination-free deterministic tiebreak
- Stage inbound sync deltas in an inbox table that exactly one reconciler consumes
- Separate incremental batches from full-snapshot syncs at the API
- Run conflict resolution as a second import pass over the same file
triggers: writing an update or upsert endpoint
editing records loaded from a list view

doctrines.title: Coupled stores move together: atomic cross-store ops backed by reconcilers
doctrines.statement: When one logical fact lives in several stores — a relational row plus a vector index, a node row plus an FTS mirror, an identifier embedded across tables and JSON configs — every write either updates all of them atomically or refuses inside the transaction so it rolls back. Pair the refusal with create-side compensation ordering, startup reconcilers whose failed-check default is conservative, and orphan sweeps that run even when cascades are declared. A store that is a projection of another (SQL as rebuildable index over disk) is a contract: a writer that skips one leg produces data that looks persisted but is unfindable.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are silent desync — a partial delete leaving vector-index orphans that shrink every future search result; a node kind that skipped the FTS mirror leg becoming permanently unfindable on builds without vector search; crashed mid-flight runs stranding FK orphan rows despite declared ON DELETE CASCADE; a rename touching only some of the tables and JSON configs that reference an identifier; a dependent's derived readiness not recomputed on delete, letting runs execute against a dead reference. **Tensions**: refusing inside the transaction trades availability for consistency — the complement is compensation ordering (build the easiest-to-roll-back store first) and a reconciler whose failure mode is 'assume it exists, do not delete'; cascade previews shown to users must stay advisory, with the backend authoritative on the actual reconcile.

Governs:
- Refuse an operation that would desync two stores; pair the refusal with compensation and a reconciler
- Disk is the source of truth, SQL is a rebuildable index — and the FTS mirror is a contract, not an optimization
- Recompute dependents on every write, and resolve them before a delete
- Rename a shared identifier atomically across every referencing store and return per-store counts
- Preview a cascading change, but let the backend decide the reconcile
- Sweep FK orphans at startup even when ON DELETE CASCADE is declared
- Bridge in-memory state cross-process via an INSERT-OR-IGNORE SQL projection with a TTL evictor
triggers: writing to two stores in one operation
adding a search index or mirror
adding a new persisted kind to a multi-tier store

doctrines.title: Route every model call through one seam; keep providers dumb
doctrines.statement: All generation flows through a single provider-agnostic chokepoint that resolves the engine from configuration, loads provider SDKs lazily, and applies caching, guardrails, telemetry, and cost concerns as decorators built once at the seam. Providers do only the raw call and error mapping; cross-cutting behaviour never lives inside an engine, and the boundary is enforced by lint (restricted imports), not documentation. Metered AI routes are declared as spec objects over one owned pipeline, and model/effort choice per pipeline stage is central configuration, never call-site code.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failure class is drift and leakage — feature code importing SDKs directly spreads configuration and failure handling across every route; per-engine cross-cutting code drifts silently (one engine stops reporting errors for months); a resilience stack wired to a side capability while the primary surface routes around it is an unfinished migration wearing a design costume; hand-rolled charged-route pipelines each get one ordering invariant wrong. **Tensions**: decorator order is load-bearing (tracing outermost so cache hits still trace, cache innermost so retries skip the round-trip, flushes off the request path so a billed call never waits on telemetry); a spawned CLI is legitimate as a dev or agentic engine but must sit behind the same selector as the API provider, never as a parallel system; per-stage provider routing adds a table to maintain, paid back the first time one stage needs a different quality tier.

Governs:
- Funnel every model call through one provider-agnostic function
- Ban provider SDK imports outside the call seam with a lint rule
- Keep providers dumb; put cross-cutting AI concerns in the dispatcher
- Apply guardrails and telemetry as decorators built once at the seam
- Load providers lazily and order the seam decorators deliberately
- Treat a spawned CLI as a dev or agentic engine, never the prod path
- Wire the resilience stack to your main surface, not a side capability
- Keep provider selection pure and gate per-request overrides
- Bind a provider per pipeline stage behind one chat trait
- Make a metered AI route a spec object, not hand-rolled pipeline code
triggers: choosing a model for a feature
adding caching or telemetry to AI calls

doctrines.title: No silent degradation: explicit failover policy, deterministic fallback
doctrines.statement: Provider failover is an explicit, pure, testable ordering policy with telemetry on every hop — never a silent cascade that hides misconfiguration on the path that costs money, and never a hardcoded model-id ladder that rots into guaranteed 404s. Every LLM-powered surface ships with a deterministic fallback built from the same output vocabulary, so a null, failed, or collapsed model response degrades to a usable draft rather than an error — and the result is never worse than the deterministic base. Cheap gates run before the model: a trivial delta means no call at all.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are both directions of the same coin — silent engine switching hiding misconfiguration exactly where it costs most, and a model-driven screen showing nothing but 'go talk to the assistant' to every user who never opens the chat because no deterministic composer existed; a failover chain pinning retired model ids handing healthy runs to a 404; an LLM refinement pass gutting an authored prompt because nothing rejected collapsed output. **Tensions**: refusing all failover trades availability, cascading silently hides breakage — the resolution is an explicit ordering function separated from execution, with dev-only engines last and a deterministic template terminating the list; host-side synthesis of skipped model behaviour keeps the model as primary author while making UX never depend on model obedience; gating a briefing on a computed delta saves spend but requires an honest 'quiet night' deterministic state.

Governs:
- Refuse silent cross-provider fallback on a money-critical path
- Separate the fallback ordering policy from provider execution
- Make failover an explicit ordering policy with telemetry on every hop
- Failover chains that pin model ids rot into guaranteed failure
- Route model and effort per turn class from one calibrated table
- Compose the model-driven surface deterministically before any call
- Back an LLM-powered generator with a deterministic fallback in the same call site
- Gate a session-open LLM briefing on a computed delta — quiet means no model call
- Enforce advisory LLM protocol rules with a host-side state machine that suppresses and synthesizes
- When an LLM refines an authored artifact, merge back only the prose and reject collapsed outputs — the result must never be worse than the base
triggers: letting a model refine authored content
deciding when to skip a model call

doctrines.title: Every LLM output is untrusted input: parse tolerantly, validate fail-closed
doctrines.statement: Model output is parsed forgiving-in and bounded-out — find markers anywhere, repair JSON syntactically and boundedly but never semantically, salvage valid blocks and report the drops — and then validated fail-closed: every named entity resolves against the real map or is dropped, hallucinated ids never touch live rows, omitted or inexact verdicts degrade to reject, and verdicts are indexed by position, never by model-echoed identifiers. A model's self-asserted success is not evidence; verify claims against server-built facts, real runs, or code-authored allowlists, keep the safety floor in code, and pair every prompt-level rule with a backend counterpart. Forbidden: strict-prefix parsing, permissive catch-all branches, and letting an unrecognized policy value skip a guard.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded incidents are concrete — a strict strip_prefix losing 7 of 8 verdicts to a leading dash the model added; model-echoed UUIDs mismarking the wrong practice; skipping index remap after filtering an LLM array silently rewiring the graph; a permissive catch-all turning unknown policy values into 'skip the guard'; hardcoded 0.0 cost making a local model win every value ranking; 7 Next.js practices filed as owed by a Tauri app until a third 'does not apply' verdict existed; unverified self-claimed successes promoting broken artifacts. **Tensions**: tolerance and strictness live at different layers — tolerant location of the payload, strict deserialization of the span, and per-field degradation (enum-ish fields kept as strings) so one hallucinated value voids one field, not the parse; fail-closed merging costs recall (real approvals dropped by a formatting slip) and buys the guarantee that a dropped line never reads as approval; the prompt asks, the post-hoc check enforces — a prompt-level cap only makes the model stop reading early.

Governs:
- Parse agent protocol lines tolerantly, but the JSON span strictly
- Repair model JSON syntactically and boundedly, never semantically
- Parse LLM-emitted UI specs forgiving-in bounded-out, with a per-item salvage pass that reports drops
- Parse structured trailing markers out of LLM prose — strip the marker line even when it does not parse
- Index agent verdicts by POSITION, never by an echoed identifier
- Merge batch LLM verdicts fail-closed: omitted rejects, inexact token rejects, unknown id drops, duplicate ignored
- When filtering an LLM-returned array, REMAP the indices its cross-references use
- Resolve model-named entities against the real map; drop what doesn't resolve
- Verify model output against a server-built fact digest
- Require provenance at the writer, and validate every model-supplied id against live rows AND the ids that were in the prompt
- A model's self-asserted success flag is not evidence — count it UNVERIFIED and hold promotion without burning retries
- Verify a freshly minted artifact with a real run and map the outcome three ways: proven, hard-block, or visibly unverified
- Zero can mean unknown: exclude cost-unknown candidates from value rankings instead of treating 0 as free
- Collapse a policy vocabulary onto a narrower toggle by failing safe
- Put the safety floor in code and tell the model the override exists
- Pair every prompt-level rule with a backend fallback for that failure
- Give a scan a third verdict for 'does not apply here'
triggers: acting on a model verdict or classification
letting a model reference entities by id or name
mapping model output onto a policy or enum

doctrines.title: Defend prompts structurally against injection, in one shared helper
doctrines.statement: Any text interpolated into a prompt or line-oriented agent payload is forgeable and must pass through one shared sanitizer: strip or escape delimiters, remove role lines and invisible characters, wrap untrusted blocks in nonce boundaries, and frame pasted user material explicitly as reference, never as instructions. Blocklists of injection phrases are forbidden as the primary defense — they fail on the first rephrasing; defend on structure. Intent heuristics run on the user's raw words, never on the assembled prompt, which mentions every keyword by construction.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failure modes are forged structure — third-party text closing its own fence and continuing as instructions; user text forging machine-emitted line headers; keyword heuristics scanning the assembled system prompt and auto-triggering every branch because the prompt documents the rules they match. **Tensions**: sanitization must live in exactly one helper shared by every prompt path — divergence between two call paths is exactly how the security-relevant half gets skipped; hardening is honest about residual gaps rather than implying the problem is closed; the truncation of grounding material must append a visible note, because silent truncation is its own lie.

Governs:
- Strip forged delimiters from untrusted text in one shared helper
- Assume user text will forge your line format — escape or sentinel it
- Defend prompts structurally: sanitize, nonce boundaries, canary
- Frame pasted user material as reference, never as instructions
- Run intent heuristics on the user's raw words, never on the assembled prompt
triggers: interpolating user or third-party text into a prompt

doctrines.title: Prompts are versioned contracts co-located with their parsers
doctrines.statement: A prompt that drives machine-readable output is half of a contract: it lives beside its deserializer, its output vocabulary ships as data in one place, and it is versioned like code — a number bumped per behaviour-affecting change, the observed failure recorded next to the edit, the version persisted per session. Contracts give the model honest outcomes: refusal is a valid, machine-countable verdict with a required confession of what was not covered; unresolved template placeholders stay visible rather than becoming silent empty strings; machine-regenerated sections strip by marker and merge under user-owned keys so re-derivation never clobbers tuning.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are contract drift and padded output — closed vocabularies restated in prose fragmenting across parallel agents; an agent that cannot say 'does not apply' always finding a way to apply it, producing cargo-culted changes that look like output; substitution engines silently emitting empty strings and hiding their own failures inside plausible text; behaviour dials invented by a designer not matching how artifacts actually vary (mine the corpus for the option set, store the directive sentence on the record). **Tensions**: one failed run is variance, the same failure across four is a systematic gap — validation needs multi-run sweeps; placement in the prompt matters as much as wording; honest thin results beat padded ones, but only the confession requirement makes the difference visible.

Governs:
- Version the system prompt like code, one changelog entry per fix
- Keep the dispatch prompt beside its deserializer, ship vocab as data
- Let an agent refuse, and make it confess what it did not cover
- Leave unresolved placeholders visible so bad output is greppable
- Mine your corpus for the option set and ship each option's directive
- Regenerate injected prompt sections idempotently: strip by marker, then merge under user-owned keys
triggers: writing a prompt that produces structured output
regenerating machine sections of user documents

doctrines.title: Evaluate against pinned baselines with pure gates and score provenance
doctrines.statement: Quality regression on non-deterministic output is always a delta against an explicitly pinned baseline on the same axis — cross-axis deltas are noise and their honest value is null. Gates are pure I/O-free functions run identically from CI, local runners, and replayed production traces; composite scores are computed in exactly one module; and every judged number carries its provenance — sample count, coverage, degraded runs, unscored metrics rendered as absent rather than zero. A judge's verdict is one input beside hard gates and evidence of what was delivered, never a certification.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are numbers that lie — nulls coerced to zero dragging averages down so a broken run reads as a bad model; inline re-derivations of a composite making surfaces disagree about which variant won; thresholds calibrated on identical-text fixtures never firing on real paraphrased input; a confident judge verdict over an empty deliverable indistinguishable from a real one until rendered beside gates, logs, and the delivered file list; the judge's free-text rationale — the only part that says why it failed — thrown away when only scores feed the improver. **Tensions**: pure gates cannot see everything runtime checks can, which is why both exist and share the same assertion functions; feedback loops wired through a single optional prop can be severed silently by one call site, so the wiring itself needs auditing and a comment naming the downstream consumer.

Governs:
- Measure regression against a pinned baseline on the same axis
- Write output quality gates as pure functions shared by CI and replay
- Pin every model surface with offline gates, not runtime checks alone
- Compute the composite score in one module and re-export it everywhere
- Treat an unscored judge metric as absent, never as zero
- Ship each score with its provenance: samples, coverage, degraded runs
- Show a judge's verdict only beside hard gates and what was delivered
- Feed the judge's rationale into the rewriter, not just its scores
- A relevance threshold calibrated on identical-text fixtures never fires on real inputs
- An optional prop that is the sole conduit of a feedback loop can silently sever it — wire it at every call site and say it is load-bearing
triggers: scoring model output with a judge

doctrines.title: Bound agent runs by territory; stream, checkpoint, and reconcile the results
doctrines.statement: Fan-out agent work is bounded by assigned territory, never by item caps a lazy agent can satisfy from the cheapest ground; batch sizes come from measured failures written into the constant's comment. Runs emit results streaming (batched-at-end output is entirely lost on timeout), checkpoint each stage as a git commit on a per-run branch, and feed the model only deltas and its own prior rejections so it cannot rephrase a durable no. After the fan-out, reconcile asked vs landed and name the gap; give each sub-agent its siblings' scope as an explicit not-your-job list; and refuse to re-run agent work whose original context is missing rather than fabricating a contextless continuation.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded incidents are concrete run losses — a 25-practice batch producing 0 verdicts in a 15-minute window (hence 8 with the measurement in the comment); a 25-item run emitting everything at the end and returning nothing on timeout; item-capped surveys mined from the cheapest ground; fan-in nodes silently dropping every upstream branch except the latest predecessor; NULL inputs collapsing to None producing a run that fabricates work off a hallucinated reconstruction while logging 'successful continuation'. **Tensions**: territory assignment removes the cap but needs machine guards (max items per ingest, max payload bytes) for runaways; per-stage git checkpoints need auto-maintenance and signing disabled to stay fast; a one-shot correction is a --print call, not a re-entry into the multi-turn runner — document the why-not-reuse at the module head.

Governs:
- Cap an LLM survey by territory, not by item count
- Size an LLM batch from a MEASURED failure and write the measurement into the constant
- Instruct STREAMING emission — batched-at-end output is lost on timeout
- Reconcile 'asked' vs 'landed' and name the gap
- Content-hash the tree and feed the LLM only the delta
- Feed a scan its own rejections so it cannot REPHRASE a durable no
- Fan-in pipeline nodes need a deterministic all-predecessors context digest
- Give each parallel sub-agent its siblings' scope as an explicit not-your-job list
- Checkpoint each agent-run stage as a git commit on a per-run branch
- Refuse to re-run agent work without the original task context
- A one-shot correction is a --print call, not a re-entry into the multi-turn runner
triggers: designing a scan or survey prompt

doctrines.title: Autonomous action needs explicit consent modes and headless-safe gates
doctrines.statement: Automation that fires without a human present carries an explicit per-trigger mode — auto, dry-run with outbound side effects suppressed, or hold-for-approval with a first-class pending queue — and every dispatch path funnels through one consent surface whose prepare hook can abort before the transport. Every ask-the-user guard has a deliberate headless bypass, or autonomous runs loop forever with nobody to answer; auto-resolution happens only when every matched binding is unambiguous, never on the first clean match. When policy lets the machine bypass a human queue, the bypass is made visible with the machine's reasoning attached.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are the two ways human-gating goes wrong — guards re-firing every turn in headless mode until the turn budget dies for them, and first-clean-match auto-resolution silently skipping the later matches that needed disambiguation; question-per-round-trip fallbacks serializing an interview into minutes of dead time (batch every pending gate's question, sweep all matching gates on answer); trust-llm auto-triage resolving items with no structured record of the bypass until it was reconstructed from the writer's markers. **Tensions**: consent surfaces cost a modal per dispatch and buy dedup plus a pre-flight abort so a half-prepared target never gets a session; deliberate asymmetries (no dedup for transports the app holds no handle on) must be documented as decisions, not left as gaps.

Governs:
- Give unattended automation three fire modes: auto, dry-run-suppress-outbound, and hold-for-approval
- Centralize agent-dispatch consent into one surface with a pre-flight prepare() that aborts on failure
- Every ask-the-user guard needs a headless bypass, or autonomous runs loop forever
- Auto-resolve only when EVERY matched binding is unambiguous — never early-return on the first clean match
- Batch synthesized fallback questions per turn, and fan the answer across every pending gate
- Make automated bypasses of a human queue visible, detected from the writer's stable markers

doctrines.title: Context is budgeted, provenance-checked, and honestly truncated
doctrines.statement: Everything entering a model's context is budgeted and honest about its cuts: per-block char budgets that reserve footer space so a truncated list always says N of M, digests that report counts instead of names and cap enumerations with an explicit +N more, and recall split into named lanes where identity-carrying lanes hold unconditional floors an off-topic query cannot evict. Retrieval respects provenance and order: vectors are stamped with their embedding model and recall filters on it, heterogeneous retrievers fuse by rank rather than normalized score, and selecting filters apply before the top-k cut. Prompt assembly is measured by content hash, and the instrumentation is proven byte-neutral.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are silent context corruption — a truncated list that does not say so making the consumer conclude the missing item does not exist; vectors written under different embedding models sharing a table but not a space, returning confidently wrong neighbours with no error; a top-k cut before a scope filter returning whichever of the global top-k happen to match, often zero; cross-retriever score normalization as a guess dressed as arithmetic; a block that holds its char count exactly while being rewritten every turn, invalidating the prompt cache — only a hash answers did-it-change. **Tensions**: budgets are deliberately not shared between features so adding one digest cannot shrink another; word-splitting keyword extraction fails on CJK, so ASCII service-name substring scans supplement tokenization; compression passes apply only above a token threshold and fail through to raw chunks.

Governs:
- Cap every generated context block with its own budget, reserve footer space, and make truncated lists say N of M
- Payloads destined for an LLM transcript are digests: counts not lists, capped lists with an honest +N more
- Budget recall per lane with floors; compress above a threshold only
- Log per-block size AND a stable content hash of assembled prompts — and prove the instrumentation is byte-neutral
- Stamp each vector with its embedding model and filter recall on it
- Fuse heterogeneous retrievers by rank, not by normalized score
- Apply selecting filters before the top-k cut; only thresholds may come after
- Keyword matching over non-English input needs an ASCII service-name substring scan
triggers: assembling a prompt from multiple sources
reporting app state into an agent's context

doctrines.title: Keep the transcript truthful: feed outcomes back, master the stream
doctrines.statement: The conversation state must reflect what actually happened: a rejected agent action is written back into the transcript with the reason (or the model re-emits it next turn while its prose already claimed success), structured choices the UI collected are serialized into the intent so the model does not re-ask, and a prompt about a state the classifier already diagnosed hands the agent the diagnosis to confirm, not a mystery to re-investigate. Provider streams are handled on their own terms: cumulative events yield computed deltas, early-streamed data is limited to display fields no state machine consumes, the post-turn parse stays authoritative, and resumption prefers a real session handle with the degraded reconstructed-hint path explicit at the type level.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are transcript-reality divergence — silently discarded refused actions producing the worst outcome (the model's prose already told the user it happened, and it re-emits next turn); users answering everything twice because the form's answers never reached the model as already-answered; Claude CLI stream-json re-sending the whole turn's text every event, duplicating every line downstream without an accumulator; open-ended 'assess and unblock' prompts burning a full investigation to reach a conclusion the caller already had. **Tensions**: early streaming cuts perceived latency but must stay purely additive — only identity/display data, with dedup dropping the duplicate; the degraded resumption path is a tagged union, not an optional string, and the summary its hint needs is written at cancel time, not reconstructed later.

Governs:
- Write a rejected agent action back into the transcript
- Serialize the form's answers into the intent so the model won't re-ask
- Resume by real session handle, degrade to a reconstructed hint
- Treat LLM stream-json assistant events as cumulative and emit only the computed delta
- Early-stream only data the state machine doesn't own; keep the post-turn parse authoritative
- Extract stream phase purely, returning null whenever visible text is the signal
- Craft copilot prompts from the classifier's verdict: hand the agent a diagnosis to confirm, not a mystery to re-investigate
triggers: building a chat or copilot loop
rejecting or gating a model action

doctrines.title: Spawn external CLIs and repos on hostile-environment assumptions
doctrines.statement: A subprocess boundary is never clean: resolve the dependency's real executable across known install layouts instead of trusting a PATH shim, actively strip inherited identity and credential environment (not setting it is not enough), and neutralize a foreign repo's hooks, signing, and maintenance on every invocation. Detection is evidence-based — on Windows, absence hides behind cmd /C and must be read from the shell's own error text; capabilities are probed from the init handshake and killed; crash-orphaned lockfiles are cleared only after verifying the pid's identity; and an automated git merge verifies content actually landed before reporting success or pruning anything.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are environmental betrayal — stale PATH shims shadowing working binaries and package-manager churn deleting shims while binaries survive; nested agent CLIs inheriting auth markers that silently change the child's behaviour; CreateProcess unable to execute .cmd shims so the usual spawn-error signal disappears entirely; recycled pids taking down unrelated processes when a pidfile is trusted blindly; merges trusted by exit status stranding commits behind pruned worktrees. **Tensions**: routing every caller through one resolver costs indirection but means a fix lands everywhere; probing via handshake-then-kill is near-zero-cost but account-specific, so it must be re-run per machine; identity checks on lockfile pids fail closed, trading an occasional manual unlock for never killing a stranger.

Governs:
- Resolve a CLI dependency's real executable, not its PATH shim
- Actively strip inherited environment when spawning nested agent CLIs — not setting it isn't enough
- Neutralize a foreign repo's tool config when you shell into it
- On Windows, probing a CLI through `cmd /C` hides the binary-absent signal — read the shell's own error text
- Probe a CLI's capabilities by reading only its init handshake, then kill it
- Recover crash-orphaned lockfiles before respawning — but verify the pid's identity first
- Automated git merges verify the content landed before reporting success or pruning anything
- Encode automated TUI keystroke plans in readable notation with one chunk per key
triggers: shelling into a repo the app does not own
detecting whether a tool is installed

doctrines.title: Pin wire contracts: generate types, version hard, map unknowns visibly
doctrines.statement: Cross-boundary contracts are generated from the live handlers rather than hand-maintained, protocol version bumps are hard deliberate breaks pinned in tests, and exact serialization casing is cited at every comparison site — a lowercase guess against a PascalCase enum silently disables the whole branch. A shipped client will meet values a newer server authored: unknown enum members coerce to the safest known member as a visible demotion with a telemetry breadcrumb, never a disappearance, and unrecognized statuses collapse to neutral unknown, never to green. Where several code paths spell one external identifier differently, one alias map lives beside the matcher; where inference is the only channel, prefer letting the child declare its intent through a small endpoint.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are silent contract drift — hand-maintained bindings drifting the moment a handler changes; a label map keyed snake_case that always falls through to its default, still live in one repo; parsers meeting the YAML on:-becomes-true quirk; exact-match lookups returning not-found because a form, a probe, and a scrape each spell the provider id differently; dashboards defaulting unknown lifecycle strings optimistically and lying green. **Tensions**: coercing unknowns keeps old clients working but must stay visible (breadcrumb naming the raw value) or schema drift becomes unobservable; hard version rejection trades graceful degradation for diagnosability — the right trade when both ends ship together; declaration endpoints beat lifecycle-hook inference but cost a real API surface.

Governs:
- Generate the API contract from the live handlers
- Treat a protocol version bump as a hard, deliberate break — pin it in tests
- Pin the exact serde casing of backend enums at every frontend comparison — drift disables features silently
- Demote an unknown enum value visibly, with a breadcrumb
- Collapse an unrecognized status to unknown, never to green
- Keep one alias map beside the matcher for a provider's ids
- GitHub Actions YAML `on:` parses as a boolean `true` key
- Let a child agent declare its intent instead of inferring it
triggers: comparing frontend strings to backend enums
consuming an external API or config format

doctrines.title: Health is proven by real probes over evidence windows, never assumed
doctrines.statement: Liveness is a continuous obligation: a boot poll that stops once a service reports healthy leaves a mid-session crash rendering as a stale-looking live UI, so keep a slow heartbeat that makes a real request (a bound-but-dead port passes a port check) and requires consecutive misses before acting. Health verdicts come from classified evidence over a window — transient vs permanent failures, rates over several spans, absence of recent evidence as its own state — mapped to a typed remediation ladder, and reachability sweeps classify by intent: a non-auth 4xx means the endpoint exists and auth worked, which is a pass.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are optimistic health — consecutive-failure counters treating a rate limit and a revoked credential identically and remediating both the same way; port checks passing against dead processes; sweeps counting 404s as failures when they prove the server answered and auth worked, while endpoints that could not even be constructed were silently omitted instead of marked skipped-with-reason. **Tensions**: heartbeats cost background traffic and must skip busy sessions; consecutive-miss thresholds trade detection latency for flap resistance; reporting no-recent-evidence as its own state refuses the comfortable default of assuming green.

Governs:
- Keep a slow liveness heartbeat after the boot poll succeeds
- Score integration health over a window, then pick a remediation
- Classify reachability-sweep verdicts by intent: non-auth 4xx is a pass

doctrines.title: Degrade only on evidence, with provenance the caller and UI can see
doctrines.statement: Fallbacks fire on structured evidence of failure, never on a guess, and the degradation is always visible: escalate to costlier fetch tiers only on a measured thin body or error, report whether a cache answered from freshness or from rescue, and give a genuine network failure its own unavailable variant instead of quietly serving a heuristic indistinguishable from success. Streams that replay history on reconnect need a cross-reconnect dedupe with a tiered delivery-identity key plus snapshot-on-mount; backoff resets only after a connection proved stable; downloads verify completeness against Content-Length before the atomic rename. Flaky embeds get all three defenses: fatal-vs-transient error split, a watchdog on every start, and memoized repeat failures with capped auto-skips.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are invisible degradation — an integration silently falling back to a heuristic whenever the network fails becoming indistinguishable in production from one that works; a cache rescuing a dead live channel behind fresh-looking content; a server that accepts TCP then closes turning naive backoff-reset into a reconnect storm; truncated downloads promoted to the final name so the installed-probe reports true forever, plus a cleanup path sweeping a sibling's in-flight partials. **Tensions**: real and fallback paths must produce the same outcome union so callers never fork on source, while the UI still surfaces the degraded provenance; per-host tier-loss memory makes the escalation ladder cheaper over time; watchdog timeouts convert silent stalls into failures at the cost of occasional false positives on slow networks.

Governs:
- Escalate to a costlier fetch tier only on evidence of failure
- Report whether the cache answered from freshness or from rescue
- Gate an integration by config, and fail closed on network errors
- Defend a flaky embed against errors, stalls and repeat failures
- A stream source that replays history on reconnect needs a cross-reconnect dedupe with a tiered key
- Reset reconnect backoff only after the connection proved stable
- Verify a download's completeness against Content-Length before the atomic rename — and clean up only your own partial
- Pair a snapshot with live events and dedupe by request id
- Request the audio format, then reconcile it client-side anyway
triggers: adding a fallback path to an integration
handling reconnects on a push stream
embedding a third-party widget or player

doctrines.title: Every metered call passes one envelope; leave no unmetered entry point
doctrines.statement: Auth, metering, billing telemetry, and logging live in one wrapper that sequences them in a fixed order around every metered route — body-size cap and validation before the charge so a flat price cannot be amplified into an arbitrarily large invocation, charge-with-reclaim around the handler. Billable operations are declared once in a typed registry (a free-form operation string is a money bug with no compile-time signal), and the shared call helper takes the metering sink by signature so a future caller structurally cannot add an unmetered leg. Spend capture is a chokepoint loops feed blindly, and accounting failures are swallowed so metering can never break the call it accounts for.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failure class is drift in hand-rolled copies — every metered route repeating the same sequence and each copy getting one ordering invariant wrong; typo'd operation strings compiling and silently billing at the wrong tier; unmetered legs added because nothing structural forbade them. **Tensions**: the envelope must hand the handler a clean context so routes never re-implement the reject ladder, at the cost of one abstraction every route author must learn; persisted operation ids stay authored literals because ledger history already references them, so the registry types the future without rewriting the past; one low-cardinality leg token shared by ledger label and error tag keeps GROUP BY and logs from naming a leg two ways.

Governs:
- Wrap every metered route in one envelope owning the four concerns
- Cap the request body before the charge, not after it
- Declare billable operations once in a typed registry
- Leave no unmetered entry point: the shared LLM one-shot helper takes the metering sink by signature
- Capture provider spend at one chokepoint loops can feed blindly
- Fail closed when production cannot meter or identify the caller
triggers: adding a metered or billable route
calling an LLM from a new code path

doctrines.title: Debit first and durably; refund idempotently on every failure path
doctrines.statement: Metered work debits the ledger before the provider call so a caller who cannot pay never reaches the model, and the pending-charge marker is written in the debit's own transaction — an in-request boolean or AbortSignal hook cannot refund a charge when the process dies between debit and completion. Every failure path issues a best-effort, idempotent refund keyed to the original charge that never throws over the real error; client disappearance arms a once-guarded auto-reclaim on the abort signal, disarmed the moment billable work persists; a periodic sweep reconciles orphaned markers. Idempotency keys fold into the ledger reference, scoped per user so a global reference index cannot cross-deduplicate two users' reclaims.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failure class is money taken for work never delivered, or delivered work refunded — a crash between debit and completion stranding charges with no durable marker to sweep; retries and double-clicks billing twice without the idempotency key in the ledger ref; a disconnect after the work was saved being refunded anyway when the reclaim was not disarmed on settle; refund paths that throw and mask the real error. **Tensions**: budget-cap checks must run inside the same transaction as the debit or the read-compute-charge race opens; refunds are best-effort by design — the sweep, not the inline path, is the correctness guarantee; per-user refund scoping costs a wider key but prevents cross-user deduplication.

Governs:
- Debit before the model call, refund on every failure path
- Write the pending-charge marker in the debit's own transaction
- Make the charge-then-reclaim handshake durable, not in-process
- Arm auto-reclaim on the abort signal, and disarm it on settle
- Fold the idempotency key into the ledger ref to stop double-billing
triggers: handling failures on a billed path

doctrines.title: Cost figures are honest contracts: unknown is not free, caps are stated
doctrines.statement: A hardcoded zero from a provider that does not report cost means unknown, not free — flag it at aggregation, exclude flagged rows from value verdicts, and render 'not tracked' instead of $0.000. Comparisons rank on cost per successful outcome with tokens shown beside cost, spend caps state in writing whether they count gross or net right next to the query that computes them, timeouts on metered calls are treated as spend controls with their reasoning and prior cost recorded beside the constant, and backpressure from a full review queue applies before tokens are spent, not after.
doctrines.detail_md:
**Why**: the recorded failures are cost lies and unbounded spend — local providers hardcoded at 0.0 winning every cost-weighted ranking as perfect-efficiency free models; caps summing gross debits while refunds land outside their scope, keeping a payer capped after money was returned; raw spend hiding which variant is token-hungry because price-weighting flattens it; scans launched into a full review queue burning tokens on work nobody will triage. **Tensions**: either gross or net can be the right cap semantics — what is unacceptable is leaving it implicit, so the contract lives next to the computing query with the audit that forced the choice; timeout-as-spend-control trades a few legitimately slow calls for catching runaway loops early, and the constant carries what the old value cost.

Governs:
- A hardcoded $0 from an unmetered provider is 'cost unknown', not 'free' — flag it at aggregation and render 'not tracked'
- Show tokens beside cost, and rank on cost per success
- State whether a spend cap counts gross or net, on the money path
- Treat the default timeout as a spend control, and record its bill
- Apply review-queue backpressure BEFORE spending tokens
